name: Zellige
summary: Moroccan tile work in which a potter glazes a square tile in one colour, fires it, and then chisels it by hand into small pieces. A worker sets the pieces face down to make a geometric mosaic.

philosophy.core_thesis: Hand-cut pieces of one-colour glazed clay make a pattern that is exact in its geometry and alive in its surface.
design_principles: Form a square tile of 10 cm by 10 cm, 12 to 15 mm thick, from local clay, and glaze it in one colour.
Chisel each fired tile with a sharp hammer into the pieces of the pattern, and cut by eye along a line.
Set the pieces face down on the drawn pattern, then pour a plaster and cement backing over them.
Base the geometry on an 8-point or 12-point star, so that every piece fits a known grid.
Limit the colours to white, green, blue, yellow, black and a warm brown, each from one oxide.
Keep the joints thin, under 2 mm, and accept a small difference in level between pieces.
Lay the mosaic as a dado up to a height of about 1.5 m, and finish the wall above it in carved plaster.
Use plain single-colour field tiles near a pattern, so that the eye has a place to rest.
anti_patterns: A printed pattern on a flat machine-made tile
A perfectly even glaze with no change of tone from tile to tile
Pastel colours that no oxide gives
Wide grout lines in a contrasting colour
Large format tiles with a sharp factory edge

form.shape: Plain square or hexagonal field tiles, chiselled mosaic panels with star patterns, fountain basins, and floors and dados in courtyards and madrasas.
form.profile: A flat face with a slight swell: each piece has a lightly irregular surface and a bevelled, hand-cut edge.
form.foot_and_rim: The tile has an unglazed back with a rough, keyed surface for the plaster. Panels end in a frame of carved plaster or cedar.
form.proportion: A field tile is 10 cm square and 12 to 15 mm thick; a mosaic piece is 1 to 8 cm across.
rules: Keep the tile square and thick enough to take the chisel.
Cut the pieces after the glaze firing, never before.
Show the slight wave of the glaze surface; do not polish the tile flat.

bodies.rule: Use a local red or buff clay that fires soft at about 950 °C and takes a thick glaze. Keep dense bodies out: they are too hard for hand cutting.

methods: pressing the tile in a wooden frame
drying the tile in the sun
chiselling the fired tile into pieces
setting the pieces face down in a drawn pattern
forming.joins: A backing of plaster and cement joins the pieces; a thin lime mortar fills the gaps.
forming.details: Chisel burrs on the back, a bevelled edge on the glazed face, small kiln marks, and a slight variation of colour in each batch.

glaze.pattern: Star and polygon patterns in green, blue, yellow, black and white, around a central 8-point star; plain single-colour tiles beside the pattern.
glaze.gloss: Glossy with a soft, uneven shine, about 60 to 85 GU.
glaze.wear: The glaze wears at the edges of the pieces and shows a light buff body; old panels turn slightly cloudy.

palette.strategy: Six glaze colours from metal oxides, set in strong contrast with a white ground.

firing.kiln: A wood or olive-stone kiln, with the tiles stacked on stilts; one firing for the biscuit and one for the glaze.
processes: a first biscuit firing of the pressed tile
dipping in tin glaze, one colour for each batch
a second firing for the glaze
firing.scale: A workshop in Fez makes a few hundred tiles for each firing, and a worker cuts about 1 square metre of mosaic in several days.
firing.signs: Three or four small stilt marks on the face or edge, a drip line, and a slight change of colour across one tile.

pieces.form: Square tile of 10 cm in plain deep green, with a soft uneven gloss
Panel of hand-cut pieces in an 8-point star in green, blue, yellow and white
Dado of about 1.5 m with a band of stars under a carved plaster wall
Hexagonal floor tile in a plain single colour for a courtyard

canonical_works.work: Zellige dado of the Attarine Madrasa, Fez
Zellige panels of the Bou Inania Madrasa, Fez

emotion.target_response: A warm, ordered calm: the viewer sees thousands of small bright pieces and feels the work of a hand in a precise pattern.

triggers: glazed clay tile in plain colours
use_cases: a kitchen or bathroom wall in plain hand-made tile
a courtyard or fountain brief in Moroccan style
a geometric mosaic brief with an 8-point star
avoid_when: the brief needs a flat machine tile
the brief needs painted figures or flowers
the brief is for a very large format panel

modifiers.how: Change to a stonepaste tile with an alkaline glaze, and set the pieces in a dome pattern with a Kufic band.
Change to a tin-glazed earthenware tile, and paint a whole picture on a flat square instead of cutting pieces.

ornament_level.note: Plain field tiles keep the low end of the range.
